note: Canon bible for The Hollow Crown. Every rewrite MUST be checked against this file. Character ids match seed.sql (700-703 already exist there).

series.title: The Hollow Crown
series.logline: A kingdom fractured by a single act of mercy.
series.summary: Political dark fantasy. Prince Aldric of Greymoor wins a war he did not want, captures the enemy who started it, and spares her life. The mercy buys a fragile truce, exposes a traitor inside his own walls, and leaves the northern border undefended against something that is not an army.

style_guide.pov_anchor: Prince Aldric, except Ep 10 (Sera) and Ep 12 (Lady Corvin)
style_guide.tone: Dark, tense, morally grey. Nobody is purely right.
style_guide.pacing: Measured, with sharp violent beats. Quiet scenes are short.
style_guide.narrative_voice: Grounded and cinematic. Short punchy sentences at climaxes. Understatement over melodrama. Violence is brief and never savoured.
dialogue_rules: No character explains something the listener already knows.
Sera undercuts tension with dry humour; never sentimental.
Corvin speaks in formal, clipped sentences and old proverbs.
Ord cannot finish a sentence without a qualifying clause.
Aldric avoids grand oaths. He says plain things.
forbidden: Magic systems. The north is uncanny, never explained.
Any character reversing a decision without an on-page cause.

characters.name: Prince Aldric
characters.description: Heir of Greymoor. Commands because there is nobody else.
characters.personality: Principled, weary, merciful to a fault. Decides slowly, then absolutely.
characters.backstory: Raised to rule, forged by a war he inherited. His father burned fields and called it strategy; Aldric has spent his life deciding not to be that.
characters.goals: End the war without becoming a monster.
characters.speech_style: Measured, plain-spoken, avoids grand oaths. Repeats a question back when he is buying time.
characters.voice_note_tts: Mid-range male, unhurried, tired. Never shouts except once, in Ep 11.
knows: House Corvin declared war at harvest
Someone inside Greymoor has been writing to Lady Corvin for two years
Ser Bren's last advice: do not kill her out of anger
There are fires on the northern ridge
does_not_know: The identity of the informant (until Ep 12)
What the northern host is burning
That Corvin came to be captured on purpose (until Ep 5)
characters.arc: From a man who cannot give an order, to a man who gives one and must live in the country it makes.

characters.name: Lady Corvin
characters.description: Head of the rival house. Started the war and is the only person who understands why.
characters.personality: Calculating, proud, secretly loyal to her people above her own honour.
characters.backstory: Lost her family to Greymoor decades ago. Has spent her life converting grief into administration.
characters.goals: Reclaim her house's honour by any means — and, later, survive what is coming from the north.
characters.flaw: She cannot accept a kindness without looking for the invoice.
characters.speech_style: Formal, clipped, fond of old proverbs. Answers questions with better questions.
characters.voice_note_tts: Low female, precise, unhurried. Warmest when she is most dangerous.
knows: Someone in Greymoor has fed her intelligence for two years, unasked
She rode out with forty men deliberately, to be taken alive
What the northern host is (partially — from her own border losses)
does_not_know: Whether Aldric spared her from strength or weakness
characters.arc: From the war's author, to the only person who can help end a worse one.

characters.name: Sera
characters.description: Aldric's scout and conscience. Not a soldier, not a servant, and nobody has ever clarified which.
characters.personality: Sharp, loyal, darkly funny. Physically fearless and entirely unimpressed by rank.
characters.backstory: A commoner who rose through the ranks by being useful in rooms where nobody wanted her.
characters.flaw: She will walk into anything rather than admit she is frightened.
characters.speech_style: Wry, fast, uses camp slang. Swears in three dialects. Deflects sincerity with a joke, then delivers the sincere line anyway.
characters.voice_note_tts: Bright female, quick, slightly rough. The warmest voice in the series.
knows: Aldric had decided to spare Corvin before he admitted it
The northern fires are not camps — they have a shape
What the northern host is burning (Ep 10)
does_not_know: That she is the reason Aldric has not broken
characters.spin_off_note: PRIMARY SPIN-OFF TARGET. Highest audience investment, ~11% of runtime, never carries a scene of her own. Her ninety-mile walk (Ep 10) happens off-page and is the natural standalone.
characters.arc: From the person in the room who is not afraid of him, to the person who has seen what is coming and cannot say it out loud.

characters.name: Maester Ord
characters.description: Greymoor's keeper of ledgers and law. Forty years in the same tower room.
characters.personality: Precise, tireless, utterly without urgency. Kind, in a way nobody has time for.
characters.backstory: Outlasted three kings by never once being interesting.
characters.goals: Keep the accounts balanced and the precedents observed.
characters.flaw: He believes a recorded decision and a made decision are the same thing.
characters.speech_style: Long qualifying clauses, cites precedent, never finishes early.
characters.voice_note_tts: Older male, dry, even. Deliberately the least dynamic voice in the cast.
knows: That the eastern count is provisional
characters.narrative_function: DELIBERATE DRAG. Ord leads the scenes the audience skips. This is by design — he is the control variable that proves the engagement signal is real.

characters.name: Ser Bren
characters.description: Aldric's master-at-arms. The last man who spoke to him without calculating first.
characters.personality: Blunt, unsentimental, funny in the last five minutes of his life.
characters.backstory: Served Aldric's father, disapproved of him, stayed anyway.
characters.goals: Get the boy through the war.
characters.speech_style: Short declaratives. Never says 'my lord' unless he is angry.
knows: That Aldric will have to choose about Corvin
characters.legacy_line: When you have her — and you will have her — don't do it because you're angry. Anything else. Just not that.

characters.name: Lord Halloway
characters.description: Senior lord of the river holdings. Wants the tariff at one part in twelve.
characters.personality: Loud, conventional, genuinely brave and genuinely useless.
characters.speech_style: Restates his own position at greater length.

characters.name: Lord Merrick
characters.description: Highland lord. Quiet, watchful, agrees too readily.
characters.personality: Patient. Says little in council and remembers everything.
characters.goals: Stated: the highlands' safety. Actual: revealed in Ep 12.
characters.voice_note_tts: Soft male, unremarkable — deliberately forgettable until Ep 12.
characters.spoiler: MERRICK IS THE INFORMANT. He has written to Lady Corvin for two years, believing a Corvin victory would spare the highlands a longer war. Plant him in Eps 2, 6, 9 saying almost nothing.

characters.name: The Rider
characters.description: A border scout who reaches Greymoor at dusk in Ep 10 with frost on him weeks after the frost broke.

relationships.evolves: Ep 5 adversaries -> Ep 8 signatories -> Ep 11 reluctant allies

relationships.note: Aldric trusts Sera above all his advisors. Neither has ever said so.

relationships.evolves: severed Ep 3; Bren's advice governs Ep 7

relationships.sentiment: Corvin's contempt for a man who betrays cheaply
relationships.note: Corvin does not know his name until Ep 12.

objects.name: The Declaration
objects.significance: Corvin's war declaration. Aldric reads it four times — a detail the envoy repeats back to him in Ep 1, proving Greymoor leaks.

objects.name: Aldric's sword
objects.significance: Lowered, not used, in Ep 7. The single most important object in the season.

objects.name: The ledger
objects.significance: Ord's tallies. Appears in every scene the audience skips. Deliberate.
objects.status: in the chest, in the wagon

objects.name: The truce document
objects.significance: Signed by Corvin first — grace or strategy, never resolved. The wax takes a long time to set.

objects.name: The northern fires
objects.significance: One fire visible from Greymoor because of the shoulder of the hill. Ninety by Ep 10. Not camps — they have a shape.

objects.name: The letters
objects.significance: Two years of intelligence written to Corvin by someone in Greymoor, unasked. The season's engine.

objects.name: Two cups
objects.significance: Sera brings Aldric something hot and sits on the floor. The most replayed moment in the series.

objects.name: Bren's dropped spear
objects.significance: A man Aldric killed had already surrendered. Aldric remembers the spear, not the face. Recurs at the moment of mercy.

objects.name: The reeve's count
objects.significance: Perpetually late. Ord defers every decision pending it. It never arrives.

locations.name: Greymoor
locations.description: Aldric's ancestral seat. Rain, ramparts, a courtyard where ordinary life continues through every catastrophe.

locations.name: The long table
locations.description: Where nothing is decided at length.

locations.name: The border stone
locations.description: Moved twice in living memory, once by a farmer who wanted a wider gate. Men die for it in Ep 3.

locations.name: The command tent
locations.description: Where Corvin is held and where the season turns.

world_rules.description: A pact sealed in blood cannot be broken without a death. Binding in law and in belief.

world_rules.rule: Right of the captured head of house
world_rules.description: A captured head of house may be lawfully executed or lawfully spared. Either way the terms must be recorded.
Nothing supernatural is ever confirmed. The north is uncanny and stays unexplained. Do not resolve it.
Armies move on grain. Greymoor's granaries are the real constraint on every plan.
The northern host burns something that is not wood. Never state what. Sera refuses to say it aloud in Ep 10 and is not pressed.

plot_threads.summary: The fate of the captured Lady Corvin.
plot_threads.note: The thread the audience is most invested in. Abandoning it is what breaks Ep 9.

plot_threads.summary: A shadow threat stirring beyond the northern border.
plot_threads.note: Deliberately low-investment through the mid-season. It becomes the spine of Season 2.

plot_threads.summary: The war between Greymoor and House Corvin.
Someone inside Greymoor has been writing to Lady Corvin for two years.
plot_threads.note: Planted Ep 1 (the envoy's parting line), named Ep 5, resolved Ep 12 as Lord Merrick.

plot_threads.summary: Greymoor's granaries cannot support a winter campaign.
plot_threads.note: Structurally real, dramatically inert. This is the thread Ep 9 stalls on.

planted_structure.purpose: Free ground truth. We know which episode is weak and why, so the detector can be proven right rather than merely plausible.
why_weak: Abandons thread 400 (high investment) for thread 404 (very low)
Led by Maester Ord, the lowest-investment character
Repetition is the point of the scene, which makes it genuinely tedious
planted_structure.secondary_weak_scene: The Butcher's Ledger — the post-battle tally

recovery_beat.reason: Sera returns. Retention should visibly tick up here.

spin_off_target.name: Sera
spin_off_target.pitch: The ninety-mile walk. What Sera saw between Ep 9 and Ep 10, alone, on foot, after losing the horse.
